english: In one trial, two fair dice are rolled. Let $A$ be the event that the first die shows an odd number, $B$ the event that the second die shows an odd number, and $C$ the event that the sum of the two numbers is odd. Five such trials are performed independently. Let $p$ be the probability that none of the events $A$, $B$, $C$ occurs in exactly two of the five trials. Then the value of $1024p$ is ______.
hindi: एक परीक्षण में दो अनभिनत पासे फेंके जाते हैं। माना कि $A$ घटना है कि पहले पासे पर विषम संख्या आती है, $B$ घटना है कि दूसरे पासे पर विषम संख्या आती है, तथा $C$ घटना है कि दोनों संख्याओं का योग विषम है। ऐसे पाँच परीक्षण स्वतन्त्र रूप से किए जाते हैं। माना कि $p$ इसकी प्रायिकता है कि पाँच में से ठीक दो परीक्षणों में घटनाओं $A$, $B$, $C$ में से कोई भी घटित नहीं होती। तब $1024p$ का मान ______ है।
solution: $P(A)=P(B)=P(C)=\dfrac{1}{2}$ and each pairwise intersection has probability $\dfrac{1}{4}$, so the events are pairwise independent; but $A\cap B\cap C=\phi$ (two odd numbers have an even sum), so they are not mutually independent
Number of trials with none $\sim B\left(5,\dfrac{1}{4}\right)$: $p=\binom{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{3}=\dfrac{10\cdot27}{1024}$
solution_full: In one trial: $P(A)=P(B)=\dfrac{1}{2}$, and $C$ occurs when exactly one die is odd, so $P(C)=\dfrac{1}{2}$.

$A\cap B$: both odd, probability $\dfrac{1}{4}$. $A\cap C$: first odd and second even, $\dfrac{1}{4}$. $B\cap C$: $\dfrac{1}{4}$. Each equals the product of the two probabilities, so $A$, $B$, $C$ are pairwise independent.

But $A\cap B\cap C=\phi$, since two odd numbers have an even sum. So $P(A\cap B\cap C)=0\neq\dfrac{1}{8}$: the events are not mutually independent, and $P(A'\cap B'\cap C')$ is not $\left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^{3}$.
By the addition theorem, $P(A\cup B\cup C)=\dfrac{3}{2}-\dfrac{3}{4}+0=\dfrac{3}{4}$, so $P(\text{none})=\dfrac{1}{4}$ (directly: none occurs exactly when both dice are even).

Across the five independent trials, the number of trials in which none occurs is binomial with $n=5$, $p_{0}=\dfrac{1}{4}$. So $p=\binom{5}{2}\left(\dfrac{1}{4}\right)^{2}\left(\dfrac{3}{4}\right)^{3}=\dfrac{10\cdot9\cdot3}{1024}=\dfrac{270}{1024}$.
Hence $1024p=270$. (Assuming mutual independence would give success probability $\dfrac{1}{8}$ and a wrong answer.)
originality_note: New: the 'none of three' probability of a pairwise-but-not-mutually independent triple is the success probability of a binomial experiment, so assuming mutual independence (1/8) instead of the true 1/4 changes the answer (way 5: pairwise versus mutual independence linked with a binomial distribution). Closest known: JEE Main 2016 two-dice pairwise-independence statement question. Different because: the independence structure feeds a repeated-trials count, so the student must compute P(none) correctly.
blueprint_concepts: Independent events; pairwise vs mutual independence of three events

concept_use.Independent events; pairwise vs mutual i: A, B, C are pairwise independent but A n B n C is empty, so P(none) = 1/4 and not 1/8.
concept_use.Binomial probability distribution: The number of trials with none of A, B, C is B(5, 1/4), and p = C(5,2)(1/4)^2(3/4)^3.
